# Microbial association networks

> Is the deterministic, depth-structured organization of inland relict communities also reflected in the architecture of microbial co-occurrence? ❓

The co-occurrence network analysis was designed and implemented by **Francisco Javier Balvino-Olvera** ([\@fjbalvino](https://github.com/fjbalvino)).

The full workflow — including ridge-regularized partial correlation inference on CLR-transformed abundances of the 200 most common taxa, balanced bootstrap resampling (500 replicates) at a fixed edge density of 0.02, topology metrics computed with `igraph`, Louvain community detection, robustness simulations, and depth-trend Spearman correlations — is documented in a dedicated directory of this repository:

👉 [**07.NetworkAnalysis**](https://github.com/DianaOaxaca/InteriorMangroves/tree/main/07.NetworkAnalysis)

There you will find the scripts, intermediate objects, and output figures corresponding to the network comparisons reported in the manuscript:

-   Inland relict vs. natural coastal sediments\
-   Inland relict vs. hydrologically impaired coastal zone\
-   Among the three inland relict localities (reproducibility across sites)\
-   Per sediment horizon within inland sites (0–15, 16–30, 31–45, 50–75 cm)
